answer: I'd like to describe a group project from my BBA, because it taught me a lot about working with other people. A memorable experience of teamwork was a group project during my university years, where we had to deliver a major presentation in just two weeks. The task was to design a complete marketing plan for a small local business and then present it to our lecturers. Our team was made up of five people with very different personalities and strengths. One was brilliant with numbers, another was a confident speaker, and one was very creative with design. At first, coordinating everyone was genuinely challenging, and there were a few [[clashes]] over how to approach things. My role naturally became that of the organiser, keeping track of deadlines and making sure everyone stayed [[on the same page]]. What made it work in the end was our willingness to [[compromise]] and play to each other's strengths. We met almost every evening in the library, often staying until it closed. As we got closer, the atmosphere became genuinely [[collaborative]], and the project came together beautifully. On the day itself, everyone played their part, and it felt like a genuine team effort. We ended up receiving one of the highest marks in the class. Honestly, the experience taught me more about cooperation than any lecture could, and I felt really proud of what we had built together. It showed me that a good team is far more than the sum of its parts, provided everyone is [[committed]] to the same goal.

followUps.q: Are you still in touch with the people from that team?
followUps.answer: With most of them, yes. We have a group chat that is still surprisingly active, and whenever a couple of us are in Dhaka at the same time, we try to meet up for dinner.

followUps.q: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
followUps.answer: It depends on the task. For detailed paperwork I like to work alone and concentrate, but for planning or solving problems, I think a team usually comes up with far better ideas.
